text:
zack: quick idea: what if instead of only windowed ranges we bake a tiny per-shard 'heatmap' that scores tensors/windows by access hotness (from evals/telemetry) so warmup can prioritize likely-hot tensors first?

anya: interesting. is the heatmap part of the manifest/sidecar or an independent hint? main win is reduced cold-latency for common prompts.

zack: propose it as an optional micro-sidecar .heat.json with entries like tensor_id -> score (0-1) and an aggregate window-hotness for transport-friendly picks. small and lossy ok.

pavan: +1 for prioritization, but some concerns: 1) privacy/leakage: telemetry-derived heatmaps could reveal prompt distributions; 2) staleness: model usage shifts, heatmap must be versioned and TTLed.

jen: on (1) we should only store aggregated, k-anonymized stats and maybe allow a "no-telemetry" signed heatmap created by runtime analysis during training infra. also include heatmap_sig to attest provenance.

mike: runtime complexity: scheduler picks ranges to fetch based on score but we must avoid starving cold tensors that are needed for rare but critical inference. need a tiered policy: top-N hot tensors prefetch, background fill for rest.

zack: exactly. policy sketch: - prefetch_top_k windows (configurable by model/fleet) - speculative fetch of next-highest windows based on available bandwidth - background fill with low priority worker threads - fallbacks keep provisional KV semantics so no provisional entries used for strict routes.

anya: perf + storage: heatmap sidecar is tiny if we aggregate at window level (e.g., 1KB per 1MB window). also useful for shrink-warmup: when capacity limited, choose minimal hot footprint.

pavan: integration with index/fastopen: heatmap could be referenced by index-hash or embedded in .fastopen header if tiny. caution: headers size limit on some CDNs. prefer sidecar URL in X-Weight-Heatmap header.

jen: metrics & safety: need new signals: heatmap_hit_rate (how often prefetched hot tensors are used), heatmap_staleness_mismatch (cases where predicted hotness didn't match actual), and a privacy audit log for heatmap generation.

mike: experiment idea: run A/B canary: baseline prefetch vs heatmap-driven prefetch; measure p95 token latency for a set of prompt traces and incremental CPU/net cost. if wins > 10% p95 with minimal extra CPU, rollout.

zack: note on ML: heatmaps may be model-and-prompt-specific. we should namespace them by route/model-version and allow multiple heatmaps per shard (route-specific hints). but that increases storage; default to global heatmap per model, optional route overrides.

anya: compatibility: mustn't alter safetensors. sidecar only. sign heatmaps with artifact signer v2 and include version+ttl. when ttl expires client should fall back to empty heatmap.

pavan: one more: tie heatmap to quantization/variant: different quant profiles may have different hotness (e.g., small attention kernels after quantization move). namespace by artifact-variant-id.

infra-bot: deploy reminder: eng-ml/heatmap-canary scheduled 04:45 UTC.

jen: ok next steps: zack to draft micro-spec for .heat sidecar (schema, signing, TTL) + warmup scheduler policy PR; we'll run the canary and collect heatmap_hit_rate + p95 latency. any blockers?

zack: I'll open RFC + small telemetry sanitizer job to k-anonymize stats. thanks all. :rocket:
